name: ob
description: The complete interface implemented by ob, the OpenBindings reference tool. One unbound contract describing everything ob does: authoring, inspecting, editing, validating, comparing, and invoking OpenBindings interfaces, plus context storage and environment management. This document carries no bindings or sources; it is the single source of truth from which the per-surface realizations (CLI via usage, server via OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/MCP) are derived, so they cannot drift. Every operation is keyed under ob's own namespace (e.g. openbindings.ob.pullSource). An operation that corresponds to a published OpenBindings interface carries that contract's operation key as an alias (openbindings.ob.setContext carries openbindings.document-store.set), and one operation may correspond to several contracts this way, as listBindingSpecs and checkBindingSpecs do.

openbindings.ob.describe.description: Return identity and metadata about ob: name, version, description, homepage, repository, maintainer.

openbindings.ob.listBindingSpecs.description: Return an advisory glance at the native binding specifications this instance can name, for display, documentation, and pickers. Presence is a support warrant and absence carries no information; support decisions use checkBindingSpecs. One operation answers the listBindingSpecs slot of every interface that has one.

openbindings.ob.checkBindingSpecs.description: Authoritatively determine support for exact, opaque binding-specification identifier tokens. This is the only operation a consumer may use to make a support decision such as source acceptance, refusal, or delegation. The result contains one verdict per unique input token in first-occurrence order. supported is always a strict boolean; true warrants that this implementation implements the specification the exact string denotes, as published. The result is deterministic for this implementation version and the operation is side-effect free. Internal patterns never extend the warranted set or match future revisions. Future optional verdict fields may annotate a verdict but never qualify supported.

bindingSpecs.description: Exact, opaque binding-specification identifier tokens to check. The array may be empty.

openbindings.ob.resolveInterface.description: Resolve an OpenBindings interface from a URL or host. Performs well-known discovery, follows redirects, and synthesizes an OBI from a raw binding spec (e.g. an OpenAPI document) when the target is not already an OBI. Returns the interface and metadata about how it was resolved.

openbindings.ob.synthesizeInterface.description: Synthesize an OpenBindings interface, optionally from binding source artifacts. Given one or more sources (e.g. an OpenAPI spec, a CLI usage spec), extracts operations, schemas, sources, and bindings into the new OBI; with no sources, produces an empty interface to author by hand.

openbindings.ob.inspectSource.description: Inspect a binding source artifact and report the bindable targets it contains, before any interface is created. Lets tooling show a user what an artifact offers.

openbindings.ob.addSource.description: Register a binding source reference on an interface and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.removeSource.description: Remove a source reference and the bindings that reference it from an interface; operations are always preserved. Returns the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.listSources.description: List the source references on an interface.

openbindings.ob.listBindings.description: List the bindings the interface declares, optionally scoped to a single operation.

openbindings.ob.addOperation.description: Add an operation with the given key to an interface and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.renameOperation.description: Rename an operation and update every reference to it across the interface — binding operation fields and binding keys following the <operation>.<source> convention. Returns the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.removeOperation.description: Remove one or more operations and their bindings from an interface and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.listOperations.description: List the operations on an interface, optionally filtered by tag.

openbindings.ob.mergeInterfaces.description: Selectively apply changes from one interface (or from the target's own sources) into another, and return the merged interface alongside a report of what was applied and skipped.

openbindings.ob.validateInterface.description: Validate an OpenBindings interface document against the specification. Reports whether it is valid, the declared spec version, and any problems. A document declaring a spec version newer than the tool supports is refused in every mode (OBI-T-04); strict mode additionally rejects unknown (non-x-) fields.

openbindings.ob.compareInterfaces.description: Structurally compare two interfaces (or one interface against what its sources produce) and report the differences per operation and metadata field, including cross-source drift.

openbindings.ob.reportCompatibility.description: Report whether a candidate interface conforms to a target interface, as an ob-comparison-report/v1 document: paired operations with directional schema verdicts and findings, a summary verdict, coverage, and category counts. A report, not a binary verdict. The target rides the report's left side, the candidate its right.

openbindings.ob.invokeBinding.description: Invoke a resolved binding via a typed bidirectional I/O frame stream (the binding-invoker frame protocol). The caller streams BindingInvokerInputFrame messages (one `open` carrying the BindingInvocationInput, zero or more `input`, one `close`); the service streams BindingInvokerOutputFrame messages back (zero or more `output`/`input_closed`, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`). One shape covers unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional bindings; cardinality is observed by how the caller drives the frames. Missing runtime context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error carrying ContextRequiredDetails, before any output and any side effect.

openbindings.ob.prepareBinding.description: Preflight a binding: report the context it would require before invocation, without invoking it or causing side effects. Returns ContextRequiredDetails the runtime can resolve proactively, or null when requirements cannot be determined statically. Advisory; invokeBinding's reactive CONTEXT_REQUIRED error is authoritative. When context is supplied, reports only the requirements still unsatisfied by it.

openbindings.ob.invokeOperation.description: Invoke an operation on an interface via a typed bidirectional I/O frame stream (the operation-invoker frame protocol). Unlike invokeBinding, the caller names an operation (or a specific binding) on a supplied interface, and the invoker resolves the name, selects a binding, validates against the operation's schemas, applies its transforms, and drives the underlying binding invoker. The frame shape mirrors invokeBinding exactly: one `open` carrying the OperationInvocationInput, then input frames and a close; output frames plus a terminal complete or error. Cardinality is observed, not declared, so a request/response and a streaming binding can satisfy the same operation identically. Missing context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error before any side effect.

openbindings.ob.prepareOperation.description: Operation-level preflight: report the context invoking an operation would require, without invoking it or causing side effects. The by-reference counterpart to prepareBinding. Resolves the named operation (or binding) on the supplied interface to a concrete binding and reports that binding's ContextRequiredDetails, or null when requirements cannot be determined without invoking. Returning null is always conformant. Advisory: invokeOperation's reactive CONTEXT_REQUIRED is authoritative. When context is supplied, the result reports only the requirements still unsatisfied by it.

openbindings.ob.getContext.description: Get the stored context for a key. Returns the unified context payload (credentials, headers, cookies, environment, metadata in a single opaque map), or null when no context matches. Lookup on URL keys is hierarchical, like invocation-time matching: the exact key wins, then the store walks up the URL path to the most specific stored prefix. Exact keys behave as a plain document get, so the document-store alias holds.

openbindings.ob.setContext.description: Create or replace the context for a key. The supplied value fully replaces any existing context (full replacement, not partial update).

openbindings.ob.removeContext.description: Remove the stored context for a key. Deleting an absent key succeeds.

openbindings.ob.listContexts.description: List metadata-only summaries for stored contexts; never returns stored context values. Completes the context surface with listing and inspection: the generic document-store substrate these contexts are stored under (satisfied by getContext/setContext/removeContext) standardizes only opaque get/set/delete, so this management view is ob's own.

openbindings.ob.registerDelegate.description: Register a delegate — any referenceable OpenBindings interface (an exec: or http(s) location) that ob may route operations to. ob resolves the location to the delegate's OBI and records a snapshot: the operation identifiers it carries (keys and aliases), a content digest pinning the resolved document, and what ob derives for its own routing — which of ob's format capabilities the delegate satisfies (checked by conformance, not name-matching) and the formats it handles. Registration fails when the location cannot be resolved to an interface. Re-registering a location re-resolves and replaces the snapshot; the registrar's preferences persist unless a new preference is supplied. An OBI carrying none of ob's three format capabilities registers successfully but is inert for ob; registration warns.

openbindings.ob.unregisterDelegate.description: Remove a registered delegate by its location. Idempotent: unregistering a location that is not registered succeeds.

openbindings.ob.listDelegates.description: List every registered delegate — the self-delegate included — with the operations each carried when last resolved, the capabilities and formats ob derived for routing, and its selection preferences.

openbindings.ob.resolveDelegate.description: Resolve an operation to the registered delegates that carry it — those whose interface answers to the operation's key or an alias — ordered by effective preference: the per-operation override when set, else the delegate-level preference, else the baseline; ties favor the self-delegate, then registration order. Returns candidates only; it does not invoke anything, and ob's routing applies its own narrowing (format support) on top.

openbindings.ob.resolveDelegateForBindin.description: Report which delegate ob's routing would select for a format token, and the capabilities it offers for it — ob's format-narrowing diagnostic, layered on top of the operation-keyed resolveDelegate.

openbindings.ob.getDelegateRequirements.description: Return the exact operation subset a delegate must satisfy to provide an ob capability (invoke → listBindingSpecs + checkBindingSpecs + invokeBinding, synthesize → listBindingSpecs + checkBindingSpecs + synthesizeInterface, inspect → listBindingSpecs + checkBindingSpecs + inspectSource). Definitions are derived from immutable published interfaces bundled with this ob release. Correspondence is per operation, so unrelated operations from the same published interface are not imposed on a delegate.

openbindings.ob.setDelegatePreference.description: Set or clear a delegate's selection preference (higher = more preferred; 0 is the baseline; negatives rank below it; null clears). Without an operation, sets the delegate-level default; with one, sets that operation's entry in the delegate's preference index. ob additionally accepts a binding-source format scope on an operation entry — how synthesis of one format can prefer one delegate while everything else prefers another. Preference governs the order resolveDelegate returns candidates in; routing applies OBI-T-09's selection semantics to delegates — ob's own narrowing, not a spec rule — with effective preference the per-operation value, else the delegate-level value, else 0. Returns the updated summary.

openbindings.ob.initializeEnvironment.description: Initialize an OpenBindings environment (a local .openbindings/ directory, or the global one with global) and return the created environment's status.

openbindings.ob.reportEnvironmentStatus.description: Report a snapshot of the active OpenBindings environment (the .openbindings/ directory): whether it is local or global, its path, the number of delegates it holds, and the number of contexts in the user's context store (contexts are user-scoped, not per-environment).

openbindings.ob.reportInterfaceStatus.description: Report an interface's status against its sources: per-source sync state (in-sync, tracked, what a pull would change) and the source-owned vs hand-authored breakdown of its operations and bindings. Read-only — distinct from pullSource (which re-derives and writes) and from compareInterfaces with fromSources (which reports raw differences).

openbindings.ob.startServer.description: Start a local server that exposes ob's operations over HTTP and the binding-invoker frame protocol, optionally adding HTTPS. A foreground, environment-local operation; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

openbindings.ob.startMCPServer.description: Serve an interface URL as an MCP server, exposing its operations as MCP tools (named by the sanitized full operation key) over stdio or HTTP. To bridge several services, compose them into one aggregate interface first. A foreground, environment-local operation, the MCP sibling of startServer; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

openbindings.ob.codegen.description: Generate a typed invoker for an interface in a target language (TypeScript or Go). The output is an invoker over the cardinality-agnostic handle, not a cardinality-specific client.

openbindings.ob.conform.description: Scaffold a target interface so it conforms to a reference interface: add the operations the reference requires and reconcile mismatches, returning the updated target and a report of each change. With dryRun, reports the changes without applying them.

openbindings.ob.demo.description: Start the bundled demonstration servers (HTTP and gRPC) that showcase one interface satisfied across multiple binding formats. A foreground, environment-local operation, like startServer; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

openbindings.ob.addOperationAlias.description: Declare satisfaction alias(es) on an operation (OBI-T-12) and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.removeOperationAlias.description: Withdraw satisfaction alias(es) from an operation and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.listOperationAliases.description: List the correspondence map — each operation and the interface operations it corresponds to via aliases.

openbindings.ob.pullSource.description: Derive operations and bindings from registered sources into the interface — create on first pull, overwrite + prune source-owned objects on later pulls, leave hand-authored objects untouched. Returns the resulting interface document plus the change log of affected operation and binding keys.

openbindings.ob.purifyInterface.description: Strip x-ob vendor metadata from an interface, yielding a spec-only document suitable for publishing.

openbindings.ob.setOperation.description: Edit an existing operation's fields (description, idempotency, deprecation, schemas, tags) and return the modified interface. A source-owned operation requires own=true (detaches first).

openbindings.ob.detachOperation.description: Convert a source-owned operation into a hand-authored one (so pull no longer overwrites it) and return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.setOperationCodegenName.description: Set (or clear) the symbol name 'ob codegen' emits for an operation, stored in the operation's x-ob.codegenName metadata, and return the modified interface. The operation key is unchanged; the override survives source pull and is stripped by purify.

openbindings.ob.setOperationOutputSchema.description: Elect an operation's real output schema (the non-detaching remedy for a floor-stamped synthesis), writing it into the operation's output and stamping an x-ob election marker, and return the modified interface. The marker survives source pull (re-applied onto each fresh derivation; a grown, non-floor-stamped source schema wins and displaces it) and is stripped by purify.

openbindings.ob.bindOperation.description: Attach a source selector to an existing operation (preserving the operation's key) and return the modified interface. Warns and optionally scaffolds transform stubs on a shape mismatch.

openbindings.ob.unbindOperation.description: Remove one exact binding, or the binding identified by operation and source, without removing the operation; return the modified interface.

openbindings.ob.newInterface.description: Create an empty interface document (core fields + empty operations map) and return it.

openbindings.ob.setMetadata.description: Edit an interface's top-level metadata (name, version, description) and return the modified interface.

InterfaceInput.description: Wraps the interface document an operation acts on.

SoftwareIdentity.description: Identity and metadata for a piece of software.

BindingSpecInfo.description: Information about a supported binding specification.

bindingSpec.description: Binding specification identifier, exact and opaque (e.g., openbindings.openapi@1, openbindings.mcp@1).

description.description: Human-readable description of this binding specification.

BindingSpecVerdict.description: Authoritative support verdict for one exact binding-specification identifier. Future optional fields may annotate this verdict but never qualify or soften supported.

bindingSpec.description: Exact binding-specification identifier token as supplied by the caller.

supported.description: Strict support verdict. True warrants that this implementation implements the specification denoted by the exact bindingSpec string, as published; false is an unqualified refusal.

address.description: Base URL or host to resolve from (e.g. https://api.example.com or localhost:8080).

synthesizedFrom.description: The binding-format token the interface was synthesized from (e.g. openapi@3.1) when the target was not already an OBI; absent for native OBIs.

resolvedUrl.description: The URL the interface document (or the source spec it was synthesized from) was ultimately fetched from.

Source.description: A binding source (binding-specification identifier plus location or content), as an OpenBindings document carries it. Open to extension fields so a document's source entry forwards verbatim.

bindingSpec.description: Binding specification identifier governing this source.

location.description: Absolute address of the source, per its binding specification (core OBI-D-05).

content.description: Embedded source-artifact representation, per its binding specification.

SynthesizeInterfaceSource.description: A binding source to synthesize an interface from.

bindingSpec.description: Binding specification identifier governing this source.

name.description: Key name for this binding source in the output.

location.description: Location to fetch content from (path or URL).

outputLocation.description: Location to reference in the output.

embed.description: If true, embed content inline in the output.

SourceInspection.description: Inspection result for a binding source artifact. Its inventory boundary is the targets admitted by the governing binding specification, not every interaction in the upstream artifact.

exhaustive.description: True when targets is the complete list of targets admitted by the governing binding specification. False means more admitted targets may exist and requires limitation evidence.

BindableTarget.description: A target admitted by the source's governing binding specification that can be framed as an OpenBindings operation. Any included framing is a sound projection of this same target.

selector.description: Selector string a conforming binding entry can use under the governing binding specification.

operationKey.description: Suggested operation key for this target.

Operation.description: An operation definition as it would appear in an interface.

input.description: JSON Schema for the new operation's input.

output.description: JSON Schema for the new operation's output.

idempotent.description: Whether the new operation is idempotent.

aliases.description: Satisfaction aliases — other interfaces' operation keys this operation also answers to (OBI-T-12).

fromSources.description: Derive the source side from the target's own binding sources.

only.description: Scope to a specific source key (requires fromSources).

excludeOperations.description: Exclude these operations from the merge.

opsOnly.description: Graft operations only (no bindings or source entries) — the adopt-keys satisfaction strategy.

noBindings.description: Don't graft bindings (operations and their referenced sources still come).

noSources.description: Don't graft source entries (operations and bindings still come).

dryRun.description: Whether this was a preview run (changes reported, not applied).

strict.description: Additionally reject unknown (non-x-) fields. A spec version newer than the tool supports is refused in every mode.

version.description: The spec version the document declares.

fromSources.description: Compare the baseline against what its binding sources produce.

only.description: Scope to a specific source key (requires fromSources).

DiffReport.description: The differences between two interfaces (or an interface and what its sources produce). Empty operations, metadata, and drift means they are identical.

DriftEntry.description: One operation key produced by multiple sources with differing schemas.

CompatibilityReport.description: An ob-comparison-report/v1 document. The target interface rides the report's left side, the candidate its right; operations are paired by key+alias resolution (OBI-T-12) and judged directionally. A report, not a binary verdict: the summary verdict is compatible, incompatible, or indeterminate. Reserved section arrays (schemas, metadata, sources, bindings, transforms, security) accompany operations.

profile.description: Schema comparison profile and hash (e.g. OB-2020-12@local).

inputs.description: Provenance descriptors for the two compared documents.

counts.description: Finding counts keyed by finding kind.

operations.description: Per-operation deltas: pairing status (paired, only_left, only_right), directional input/output schema verdicts, and findings.

suppressed.description: Findings suppressed by suppression rules, with the rule that matched.

ComparisonInputDescriptor.description: Provenance of one compared document: where it came from and its canonical content hash.

source.description: Locator kind (e.g. file, http, exec); empty for inline documents.

BindingContext.description: Opaque context supplied by value for one binding invocation. The contract neither requires nor exposes a context store; callers may assemble this object from per-call values, durable state, a credential broker, or any other source before invocation. The general named-credential field is 'credentials': an object keyed by a requirement's nonempty 'name'. For auth.bearer and auth.apiKey its named value is a string; for auth.basic it is an object with username and password; for auth.oauth2 it is an object whose accessToken is the applying credential and whose refreshToken, expiresAt, and clientSecret are optional lifecycle values. Unnamed or unambiguous single-scheme conveniences remain 'bearerToken', 'apiKey', 'basic', and 'accessToken' / 'refreshToken' / 'expiresAt'; the historical 'apiKeys' named map remains accepted for auth.apiKey. Well-known transport fields: 'headers' / 'cookies' / 'environment' (objects with string values) and 'metadata' (object with arbitrary values). Well-known configuration field: 'configuration' (object), keyed by configuration-point name and interpreted by the specification that defines each point. A config.value requirement's relative JSON Pointer path addresses within configuration[point]; an empty path addresses the entire point. The operation-invoker contract defines configuration.selection as an ordered array of binding-key strings. Implementations and callers MAY add fields for session state, consent, or other runtime data; consumers SHOULD ignore fields they do not recognize unless the governing binding specification says otherwise. Every value in credentials and the single-scheme credential fields is secret, and any other field may also be secret according to its requirement family, binding specification, or application policy.

BindingInvocationInput.description: Initial payload carried by the `open` input frame: identifies the binding to invoke and provides context.

BindingInvokerInputFrame.description: One frame from the caller into invokeBinding. The caller streams a sequence: exactly one `open` frame first (carrying the BindingInvocationInput), then zero or more `input` frames carrying values to deliver to the underlying binding, then exactly one `close` frame signaling no more input.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

value.description: One input value, opaque at this layer.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller signals that no more input frames will be sent. Idempotent.

BindingInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from the service back to the caller. The service streams a sequence: zero or more non-terminal frames (`output`, `input_closed`) followed by exactly one terminal frame (`complete` or `error`).

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

value.description: One output value, opaque at this layer.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: Binding has closed the input side from its end (e.g., a unary binding closes input after the first read). Subsequent caller `input` frames are ignored (never written; see rule 3). The invocation continues; outputs may still flow.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

OperationInvocationInput.description: Initial payload carried by invokeOperation's open frame: the interface to act on and which operation (or specific binding) to invoke, plus context.

operation.description: Operation key to invoke. A binding is selected automatically.

binding.description: Binding key to invoke; the operation is derived from it. Mutually exclusive with operation.

OperationInvokerInputFrame.description: One frame from the caller into invokeOperation. Same shape as the binding-invoker input stream, with the open frame carrying an OperationInvocationInput: exactly one `open` first, then zero or more `input` frames, then exactly one `close`.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the operation. Validated against the operation's input schema.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller signals no more input frames will be sent. Idempotent.

OperationInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from invokeOperation back to the caller. Same shape as the binding-invoker output stream: zero or more `output`/`input_closed` frames, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`. Each output is validated against the operation's output schema.

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the operation.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The operation has closed the input side from its end. Subsequent caller input frames are ignored. Outputs may still flow.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

InvocationError.description: Minimal unsuccessful-completion record carried by an `error` output frame. The frame kind is the portable failure signal. Only codes named by a rule of this interface, its operation-invoker peer, or the governing binding specification have portable semantics; other strings are open extension or implementation identifiers. Codes defined by either invocation interface are reserved to their defined meanings and MUST NOT be redefined by a binding or implementation. Other governed codes SHOULD use collision-resistant identifiers. ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED is the generic fallback when no more specific governed meaning exists; it means only that the interaction completed unsuccessfully, and carries no protocol category, blame, retryability, side-effect, authentication, authorization, or availability semantics.

code.description: Machine-readable error code. This interface owns CONTEXT_REQUIRED, ERR_CANCELLED, ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL, ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED, and ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED.

data.description: Optional portable JSON data associated with the unsuccessful completion. A rule defining `code` may define its structure and semantics; otherwise, the governing binding specification may use it to preserve an opaque application-authored failure value. For CONTEXT_REQUIRED, this is a ContextRequiredDetails object. Presence is significant: an absent member means no portable associated value, while an explicit null is a present JSON null value. Statuses, headers, trailers, envelopes, raw debugging bytes, exception prose, stacks, and implementation evidence do not belong here unless they are themselves application data under an explicit governing rule.

ContextRequiredDetails.description: The `data` value of an InvocationError whose `code` is CONTEXT_REQUIRED, and the return shape of this contract's preflight operation. Enumerates the context the invoker needs before it can proceed. `alternatives` are disjunctive: satisfying ANY one suffices. The `requirements` within a single alternative are conjunctive: ALL must be satisfied. This OR-of-AND shape captures real authentication semantics such as 'OAuth2 OR (apiKey AND clientCert)', which a flat list cannot. A challenge is a scope, not a hint: a caller that resolves it MUST provision only the context needed for one selected alternative and MUST NOT disclose unrelated credentials. The interface supplies context by value and exposes no context-store access.

target.description: Opaque identifier for the concrete destination or context scope asserted by the invoker. A runtime MAY use it to scope resolution or reuse. Before releasing a reusable secret on an assertion from outside its trust boundary, a resolver MUST validate that assertion against independently derived information; an in-process resolver MAY deliberately include its co-located invoker in the trust boundary. Interpretation, normalization, hierarchy, key derivation, and persistence policy are otherwise outside this contract.

alternatives.description: Disjunctive set of ways to satisfy the requirement. A resolving caller selects one alternative whose every requirement it can resolve and provisions only the context needed for that alternative, never unrelated credentials.

requirements.description: Conjunctive set: every requirement in this alternative must be resolved for the alternative to be satisfied.

ContextRequirement.description: One prerequisite that must be satisfied before a binding can be invoked. `type` names the requirement family; the remaining fields are type-specific. A named well-known `auth.*` requirement resolves at BindingContext.credentials[name]: a string for `auth.bearer` and `auth.apiKey`, a username/password object for `auth.basic`, or an OAuth object beginning with accessToken for `auth.oauth2`. Unnamed or unambiguous single-scheme requirements use the corresponding bearerToken, apiKey, basic, or flat OAuth conveniences; historical apiKeys[name] remains accepted for `auth.apiKey`. OAuth requirements may carry flow fields such as grantType, authorizeUrl, tokenUrl, and scopes. The `config.value` family carries a configuration value a binding needs but the artifact does not supply: it carries 'point' and a relative JSON Pointer 'path' (plus an optional engine-asserted 'schema') and resolves within BindingContext.configuration. Other families (e.g. 'approval.user', 'account.link') resolve into their own context fields. Resolution architecture and value secrecy beyond the always-secret credential fields are determined by the requirement family, governing binding specification, and caller.

type.description: Requirement type identifier, e.g. 'auth.bearer', 'auth.oauth2', 'auth.basic', 'auth.apiKey', 'approval.user', 'config.value'. An unrecognized type is unsatisfiable by a runtime that has no way to satisfy it. An invoker may surface an artifact-defined scheme as an extension requirement only when it knows how the resulting context will be applied faithfully; an invoker that cannot represent or apply a prerequisite refuses before dispatch rather than emitting a satisfiable-looking challenge or attempting the interaction without it.

name.description: The scheme name as the source artifact declares it (e.g. an OpenAPI securitySchemes key). Distinguishes multiple requirements of the same family and keys scheme-scoped lookup in BindingContext.credentials.

point.description: config.value only: the binding-specification configuration point the value belongs to ('server', 'address', a family's decode point, …).

path.description: config.value only: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer relative to configuration[point]. The empty pointer addresses the whole point; '/variables/region' addresses a nested member; '/value' addresses a member literally named value.

schema.description: config.value only: an engine-asserted JSON Schema for the value addressed by point and path. Derived from the source artifact where the artifact speaks, supplied by the binding-specification implementation where that specification pins a shape, and absent where nothing does; absence means the value is unconstrained. An 'enum' declares the closed admissible set and satisfaction validates against it; 'examples' are advisory suggestions and an off-list value remains valid.

description.description: Human-readable description shown to a user or operator during resolution (e.g. an approval prompt message).

durable.description: Whether resolved context for this requirement MAY be persisted and reused for later invocations (true), or MUST be satisfied freshly and MUST NOT be persisted or reused (false). Defaults to false. This permission does not require persistence or prescribe a store, key, or reuse policy.

Context.description: Opaque per-target context payload: credentials, session state, headers, cookies, environment, metadata, or any other invoker-managed state. Well-known fields include bearerToken, apiKey, basic, headers, cookies, environment, metadata.

ContextSummary.description: Non-secret metadata about a stored context entry. Never includes secret values.

url.description: Context store key (normalized API origin or other stable identifier).

loadError.description: Set if the entry could not be parsed.

location.description: Delegate location: the exec: or http(s) URL of the delegate's OpenBindings interface. Also the delegate's registration identity.

preference.description: Initial delegate-level selection preference (higher = more preferred). May be changed later with setDelegatePreference.

DelegateSummary.description: A registered delegate: its identity, the snapshot of what it carries, ob's derived routing data, and its selection preferences.

name.description: Display name: the delegate OBI's name, or one derived from its location.

location.description: The reference the delegate is registered under (exec: or http(s) URL). The self-delegate's location is "ob".

operations.description: Every operation identifier the delegate answers to — the keys and aliases its interface declared when last resolved. A snapshot: re-registering the location refreshes it.

contentHash.description: Digest of the delegate's interface document as last resolved (sha256: over its RFC 8785 canonical form). Pins the snapshot; opaque — compare for equality, don't recompute.

capabilities.description: Which of ob's format capabilities the delegate satisfies, checked by conformance at registration.

bindingSpecs.description: The formats the delegate reported handling when last resolved.

preference.description: Delegate-level selection preference — the default for every operation it carries. Higher is more preferred; absent is the baseline.

operationPreferences.description: Per-operation preference overrides, keyed by operation identifier. The override replaces the delegate-level preference when resolving that operation.

bindingSpecPreferences.description: Preference overrides scoped to one (operation, format) pair — ob's extra granularity beyond the delegate-manager contract's per-operation index.

builtin.description: True for ob's own native handling — the self-delegate.

operation.description: The operation identifier a delegate is needed for.
The requested operation identifier, echoed back.

candidates.description: Registered delegates that carry the operation, ordered by effective preference, best first. Empty when none carry it.

bindingSpec.description: Binding specification identifier to resolve to a delegate.

name.description: Display name of the delegate ob's routing would select.

capabilities.description: The capabilities the delegate offers for this format.

builtin.description: True when ob's own native handling is selected for the format.

global.description: Initialize the global environment (the openbindings directory under the user config dir) instead of a local .openbindings/ directory.

delegateCount.description: Number of registered delegates in this environment.

contextCount.description: Number of contexts in the user's context store (user-scoped, not per-environment).

tls.description: Also serve HTTPS using a locally generated CA without modifying system trust.

trustLocalCA.description: Install the locally generated HTTPS CA into system trust; implies tls and may require administrator approval.

url.description: Interface URL to expose as an MCP server (an OBI, a well-known discovery base, or a raw binding spec). Compose an aggregate OBI to bridge several services.

port.description: HTTP port when transport is http (default 8080).

url.description: Base URL the server is listening on.

language.description: Target language for the generated invoker.

package.description: Go package name (Go only; default derived from the interface name).

ConformInput.description: conform input: `interface` is the reference contract whose operations `target` must satisfy; `target` is the interface scaffolded to conform, returned modified as `interface` in the result.

dryRun.description: Report the changes without applying them.

ConformResult.description: The conformed target document plus a report of each change made or proposed.

interfaceName.description: Display name of the reference interface being conformed to.

modified.description: Whether the target was changed (false under dryRun or when already conformant).

ConformAction.description: A single change conform made or would make to the target.

operation.description: The operation key the change concerns.

action.description: scaffold (add a missing operation), replace (update a drifted one), skip, or compatible (already conforms).

SourceListEntry.description: A source from the interface's sources map, with its key.

key.description: The source's key in the interface's sources map.

operation.description: Scope the listing to a single operation's bindings.

BindingListEntry.description: A binding from the interface's bindings map, with its key.

key.description: The binding's key in the interface's bindings map.

source.description: The source key this binding invokes.

selector.description: The binding-specification selector into the source.

preference.description: The author-declared selection preference, when set.

inputTransform.description: Whether the binding declares an input transform.

outputTransform.description: Whether the binding declares an output transform.

OperationListEntry.description: An operation from the interface's operations map, with its key and the bindings that realize it.

key.description: The operation's key in the interface's operations map.

bindings.description: Keys of the binding entries that realize this operation.

MergeEntry.description: One operation-level change in a merge, and whether it was applied.

operation.description: The operation key the change concerns.

action.description: The merge action for this entry (e.g. add, update, conflict).

location.description: Delegate location: the exec: or http(s) URL of the delegate's OpenBindings interface.

DelegateCapability.description: One of ob's three binding-specification handling needs, derived from a minimal operation subset of published interfaces: invoke (binding-invoker), synthesize (interface-synthesizer), inspect (source-inspector plus the interface-synthesizer support query). A delegate offers whichever subsets it satisfies; operations outside a subset remain independent capabilities.

bindingSpec.description: Format token the delegate handles (e.g. grpc, openapi@3.1).

description.description: Human-readable description of the format, when the delegate provides one.

BindingSpecPreference.description: A preference override scoped to one (operation, format) pair — ob's extra granularity beyond the delegate-manager contract's per-operation index. It replaces both the delegate-level and the per-operation preference when resolving that operation for that binding-source format.

operation.description: The operation identifier this override is scoped to.

bindingSpec.description: The binding-source format this override is scoped to (e.g. grpc, openapi@3.1).

preference.description: The scoped preference value; higher is more preferred.

location.description: The reference the delegate is registered under.

preference.description: The new preference value; higher is more preferred, 0 is the baseline, negatives rank below it. Null clears: with an operation, it removes that operation's override; without one, it resets the delegate-level preference to the baseline.

operation.description: When present, the preference applies only to resolving this operation; otherwise it is the delegate-level default.

bindingSpec.description: Optional binding-source format scope for an operation entry (requires operation) — ob's extra granularity beyond the delegate-manager contract.

ProvenanceKeys.description: Keys split by provenance: source-owned (derived from a source by pullSource) vs hand-authored.

SourcePullOutput.description: The result of a `source pull`: the resulting interface document plus the change log — the source-owned operations and bindings added, updated, or pruned, the sources pulled and skipped, and any warnings.

SourceStatus.description: Drift status of one source on an interface: what `ob source pull` would add/update/remove, plus custodial drift on hand-authored bindings whose target is gone.

inSync.description: Whether the source would change nothing and has no custodial drift.

tracked.description: Whether ob tracks this source via x-ob provenance metadata (written by addSource or synthesizeInterface). Untracked sources are hand-authored; pull skips them.

custodial.description: Hand-authored bindings whose source target no longer exists.

InterfaceStatus.description: An interface's read-only status against its sources: per-source sync state plus the source-owned vs hand-authored breakdown of its operations and bindings.

operation.description: The operation's key or any existing identifier.
The operation's key or any existing identifier.
Scope the satisfaction map to a single operation.

OperationAliasEntry.description: An operation and the interface operations it corresponds to via aliases.

sourceKeys.description: Sources to pull; empty means all registered sources.

operation.description: The operation's key or any identifier.

input.description: Replacement JSON Schema for the operation's input.

output.description: Replacement JSON Schema for the operation's output.

own.description: Take ownership of a source-owned operation (detach) before editing.

operation.description: The operation's key or any identifier.
The operation's key or any identifier.

codegenName.description: The symbol name 'ob codegen' should emit for this operation. Omit (or send empty) with clear=true to remove the override.

operation.description: The operation's key or any identifier.

outputSchema.description: The real output schema to elect. Omit with clear=true to remove the election.

operation.description: The operation's key or any identifier.

preference.description: Author preference signal (higher = more preferred); this field does not itself select a binding.

inputTransform.description: Inline JSONata transforming operation input to binding input.

outputTransform.description: Inline JSONata transforming binding output to operation output.

transformStub.description: Scaffold identity transform stub(s) on shape mismatch.

force.description: Overwrite an existing binding for this operation and source.

UnbindOperationInput.description: Select exactly one binding either by its exact binding key, or by the operation and source pair used by ob's conventional binding-key form. Supplying neither selector, an incomplete pair, or both selectors is refused.

operation.description: The operation's key or any identifier. Used with source when binding is absent.

source.description: Source key whose binding to remove. Used with operation when binding is absent.

binding.description: Exact binding key to remove. Do not also supply operation or source.

openbindings.description: Target OpenBindings spec version; defaults to the tool's max tested version.

InspectionLimitation.description: Machine-readable evidence explaining why a source inspection is not exhaustive.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what may be missing and why.

details.description: Optional implementation- or family-specific structured evidence.
